title: The lanterns go back up this Friday
summary: Forty stalls, one brass band and a very long string of lights. Opening night starts at 5.
content:
We spent last Saturday on ladders. Every lantern on the Row is back up, the power is run to the far end of the street, and Dottie has already started arguing with the wind about her awning.

Opening night starts at 5 on Friday and runs until the last dumpling sells out. That was 9:40 last year, so don't cut it close. Stalls open along the whole block, the Mill Street Brass Band plays at 7, and kids can paint a paper lantern at the top of the Row for free.

If you've never been, here's how it works. Start at the old feed store, eat your way down the Row, and finish at the band. Most people walk the whole block twice: once to look, and once to buy.

A few things have changed since last fall. The bike racks moved to the rail spur end, there are real bathrooms behind the hardware store now, and the lanterns over the crosswalk run on solar, so they stay lit when the power trips.

Parking fills up fast. The lot behind the old feed store is open and it's a two-minute walk. Bring cash for the smaller stalls, and bring a bag.

See you Friday. Look for the yellow lanterns.
